identity.name: INSOLATION ENERGY LIMITED
identity.sector: Solar PV manufacturing - integrated module-to-cell (forward into EPC/IPP)

one-line thesis: Fast-growing (~60% YoY) Rajasthan-based solar module maker that just moved to the main board and is using a heavily debt-funded 4.5 GW TOPCon cell + aluminium-frame backward-integration push (COD Q4 FY27) to lift EBITDA margin from ~14% toward 20%+ by FY28 — execution and working-capital/receivables discipline are the swing factors.
financial scorecard: One-offs / quality notes: receivables up 156% to INR280 cr (mgmt attributes to shift from advance-based to 45-day LC terms on larger utility orders); raw-material cost up ~190% (scale + backward-stocking 2-3 months inventory); short-term borrowing up INR100→INR300 cr (working-capital for expanded capacity); FCFF negative (-15.9% yield, growth/capex phase).
guidance (next-quarter / forward): FY27 revenue: maintain or beat ~50-60% growth (module-only basis; cell sales would be incremental).
Q1 FY27 production: "nearly similar" to Q4 (~500+ MW dispatched in Q4).
FY27 module volume: ~2 GW production & ~2 GW sales (non-DCR base); 2.5-3 GW total including DCR cells procured externally.
FY27 margin: 14-15% (small uplift from aluminium integration).
FY28: revenue >INR5,000 cr; EBITDA margin 20%+ once cell line fully ramped (Q1 FY28 full utilization).
IPP/KUSUM revenue: ~INR135 cr in FY27, ~INR300 cr in FY28.
Cell line COD: Q4 FY27; ramp to 60-70% over two quarters, full by Q1 FY28.
order book & pipeline: ~50% of FY27 capacity already booked; balance refilled monthly via dealer/distribution (Rajasthan, Delhi NCR, Haryana, MP, UP), OEM white-label, and KUSUM partners.
MoUs signed for ALMM Part 2 cell-for-module and DCR-cell sales; more MoUs expected within 1-2 months.
Third-party EPC order >INR300 cr secured last year; revenue to flow in FY27 (EPC at nascent stage end-FY26).
~45 GW+ of non-DCR tenders (pre-Oct-2025) still open in India → ~1-1.5 yr of non-DCR cell demand runway.
segment / subsidiary detail: Segment mix (FY26 capacity allocation): Utility ~65%; KUSUM ~15%; PM Surya Ghar ~5%; OEM ~5%; misc ~10%. Retail/channel ~10-15%.
DCR vs non-DCR FY26 sales: ~85% non-DCR / ~15% DCR.
Channel: 700+ partners, 25,000+ customers; Urja 4.0 partner meet; 40,000 homes solarized.
IPP/KUSUM: 325 MW AC / ~400 MW DC planned commissioning FY27; ~38-40 MW already commissioned.
growth verticals / optionality: 4.5 GW TOPCon solar cell (COD Q4 FY27) — core backward-integration / ALMM Part 2 play.
4.5 GW aluminium frame facility (commissioning Q1 FY27) — captive, margin accretive.

Wafer & ingot 4.5 GW (CZ growing tech, TOPCon G12R) — land secured (70,000 sqm / ~20 acres) at Narmadapuram; DPR in progress; capex INR1,000-1,200 cr; target ahead of ALMM Part 3 (effective 1-Jun-2028); funded mostly via internal accruals.
BESS — under evaluation only, NO capex planned (explicitly).
Exports (Europe/Africa) — not viable now, no plans.
margins & cost dynamics: Realizations (last quarter): non-DCR TOPCon INR13-14/W; DCR Mono PERC INR20-21/W; DCR TOPCon INR21-22.5/W.
RM price escalation handled via dollar-linked escalation clauses + 2-3 months back-to-back RM stocking; mgmt works on "delta" basis, partially absorbs / partially passes through.
Margin uplift path: aluminium integration (small, FY27) → cell line operational (large, →20%+ FY28).
capex / expansion: FY27 total capex ~INR2,500 cr: ~INR1,500 cr cell line (incl. ~INR180-190 cr contingency + WC; plant/machinery/building/utilities ~INR1,300 cr) + ~INR1,000 cr KUSUM IPP (300 MW target).
FY26: Sawarda Unit 3 module plant completed (INR320 cr, all 3 lines operational, 5.5 GW total module capacity).
IREDA loan INR1,134 cr sanctioned; INR340 cr drawn (FY26); 12-month moratorium, 7-yr repay; pre-COD 9.20% / post-COD 8.95%.
capital allocation: Net D/E 0.5x; long-term debt ~INR468 cr (incl. INR340 cr IREDA); peak debt ~INR1,500 cr in FY27.
>INR400 cr cash (incl. ~INR300 cr FD against undrawn IREDA).
Stated priority: fund cell+frame expansion, maintain prudent leverage & healthy ROCE; wafer/ingot to be funded largely from internal accruals once cell cash flow ramps.
risks & watch-items: Negative FCFF / negative working capital during the heavy capex phase; positive FCF only ~6-8 months post-cell-COD.
Receivables surge (+156% to INR280 cr) — debtor-day discipline as orders scale to 100-500 MW with 45-day LC.
RM price volatility / module overcapacity & price pressure (non-ALMM modules ~30 GW overhang).
Execution / commissioning timeline risk on cell line (Q4 FY27) and dependence on Chinese cell equipment (~85% industry reliance; 2-yr Chinese+Indian support contract mitigates).
Margin guidance (20%+ FY28) is back-end-loaded and contingent on full cell ramp + market pricing.
Policy dependence: ALMM Part 2 (effective 1-Jun-2026) / Part 3 (1-Jun-2028), KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar.
management quality / tone: Confident, growth-forward; promoters openly invite plant visits / analyst meets. CFO gives reasonably specific debt, capex and realization numbers. Some guidance hedged ("depends on market", "after Q1/1st June clarity"). English is non-native and occasionally loose ("550 gigawatt" is clearly 5.5 GW; "EBITDA should be 100%, 20% plus"), so figures need cross-checking against filings.
non-obvious takeaways: The 20%+ FY28 EBITDA story is fundamentally a cell self-supply margin-capture story, not a module-pricing story — module realizations are commoditizing (non-DCR TOPCon only INR13-14/W).
Quarterly revenue is lumpy by design: utility dispatches concentrate in the last month of each quarter (Dec ~INR350 cr, Mar ~INR440+ cr) — single-month run-rates mislead.
Wafer/ingot ambition pre-empts ALMM Part 3 (Jun-2028); positions INA toward full vertical integration (ingot→wafer→cell→module→frame→EPC→IPP), rare among listed Indian peers.
DCR vs non-DCR realization gap (INR20-22 vs INR13-14) shows DCR/ALMM compliance, not volume, is the real margin lever; cell line unlocks DCR participation.
qoq change log: This quarter (Q4 FY26):
Main-board listing on BSE & NSE (9-Mar-2026) — key milestone.
Q4 revenue doubled YoY to INR794 cr; FY26 INR2,146 cr (+61%), PAT INR201 cr.
Cell capex revised up INR1,300 cr → INR1,500 cr (added WC + contingency); cell COD Q3 vs Q4 FY27 messaging (MD said Q3 COD; Chairman/CFO repeatedly said Q4 FY27 operational — note the discrepancy).
FY27 module volume target revised DOWN to ~2-2.5 GW (non-DCR) from prior ~3 GW (250-275 MW/month); DCR now treated as incremental.
Aluminium frame commissioning Q1 FY27 (confirmed).
Wafer/ingot land secured (70,000 sqm), DPR started.
IREDA INR340 cr first tranche drawn.
Next-quarter watch items:
Post-1-Jun-2026 ALMM Part 2 market behaviour & pricing (mgmt flagged clarity "after Q1 / 1st June").
Receivables / debtor-day trajectory as LC-based large orders scale.
Cell line construction progress vs Q4 FY27 COD; reconcile Q3 vs Q4 COD messaging.
Q1 FY27 dispatch run-rate vs ~500 MW Q4 base.
KUSUM IPP commissioning beyond the ~38-40 MW already live (target 325 MW AC FY27).
Confirmation/finalization of wafer-ingot DPR & capex (INR1,000-1,200 cr).

themes.title: Solar PV cell-to-module manufacturing
themes.need: Solar module/cell manufacturers ride capacity ramp, ALMM/DCR protection and an order-book build-out - a manufacturing thesis distinct from firm-power/FDRE tender economics or merchant storage arbitrage. Q1FY27 quantified the DCR arbitrage: EMMVEE grew revenue 51% to INR 1,555cr with EBITDA margin up to 35.2% and PAT +103% on a 9.9 GW order book, with DCR modules earning INR 8.5-9/W of EBITDA against INR 2-2.5/W for non-DCR - a 3-4x per-watt gap that structurally separates integrated cell makers from module assemblers. The offset is order timing: SWSOLAR booked a record INR 13,000cr unexecuted order value on a landmark USD 560m Egypt win (1,000 MW solar + 600 MWh BESS) yet revenue still fell 10% YoY, and flagged that industry orders concluded only ~INR 6,400cr against the >INR 20,000cr expected, deferred by DCR/module-price uncertainty.
themes.driver: DCR cell/module capacity commissioning and the ALMM List-2 per-watt spread; domestic ordering restarting after two slow quarters (SWSOLAR); order-book conversion.
